scenes.visual: carbon and electrons through three boxes
scenes.narration: Converting pyruvate to acetyl co-A is not one reaction but three, carried out in sequence by a single complex. First comes decarboxylation: thiamine pyrophosphate grabs pyruvate, and carbon dioxide leaves from that grip. The remaining two-carbon fragment stays bound to it. Second is oxidation, where two electrons leave and the fragment is handed to the lipoamide arm. Third is transfer to coenzyme A, producing acetyl co-A. Follow the carbon across the three boxes and follow the electrons separately, because those electrons end up reducing NAD plus to NADH. Notice that each step uses its own coenzyme, and several of those coenzymes trace back to B vitamins.

scenes.visual: lipoamide arm swings between E1, E2, E3
scenes.narration: Watch the lipoamide arm make its rounds. Tethered to the E2 core, it first swings to E1 and picks up the acetyl group, becoming acetyl-lipoamide. Next, it pivots back to E2 and delivers that acetyl unit to coenzyme A. That releases acetyl co-A and leaves the arm reduced as dihydrolipoamide. Finally, it reaches E3 to be reoxidized, regenerating the disulfide so the cycle can repeat. The arm rides on a mobile lipoyl domain. Because the E2 core has twenty-four or sixty copies, all three active sites stay within reach. The intermediates never escape. They ride the tethered arm from station to station.

scenes.visual: timeline of four steps, NADH only at the last. Show the first three boxes grouped as 'build acetyl-CoA' plus a fourth box 'reset arm (E3): NADH' appearing as spoken.
scenes.narration: Put the whole mechanism on one timeline so you see where NADH is born. Three steps build acetyl co-A, and a fourth step resets the arm. Step one, decarboxylation on E1, releases carbon dioxide and makes no NADH. Step two, oxidative transfer, oxidizes the fragment and loads it onto lipoamide, still no NADH. Step three, acetyl transfer on E2, produces acetyl co-A and leaves reduced lipoamide, again with no NADH. A fourth step, on E3, resets the lipoamide arm. There, FAD reoxidizes the arm, and only that reset passes electrons onward to make NADH.

scenes.narration: Enzyme E1 is the key regulatory site of the entire complex. A kinase and a phosphatase travel with the complex as a simple on-off switch. A kinase phosphorylates E1 and inactivates it. A phosphatase removes that phosphate and reactivates it. The switch reads the cell's energy state. When ATP, acetyl co-A and NADH are abundant, signaling plenty of fuel and product, the complex is inhibited. When ADP and pyruvate accumulate, signaling demand and available substrate, the complex is stimulated. So the gateway from glycolysis to the citric acid cycle opens only when the cell actually needs to burn pyruvate.
